text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis says state will recapitalise GAN as early as 1997, with an 11 billion franc recapitalisation, and a 9 billion francs guarantee.
-- Renault carmaker launches its restructuring, closes plant in Belgium.
-- Paribas returns to profits for 1996 with a 4.35 billion franc result.
-- British Aerospace chairman says he supports Lagardere 's bid for Thomson-CSF.
-- M6 TV-channel chairman says channel has sufficient financial capability to enter digital-TV market.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Unions at Renault fear job cuts in France.
-- Insurer GAN to be privatised this year after state recapitalisation.
-- Bouygues chairman Martin Bouygues and TF1 chairman Patrick Le Lay placed under investigation for alleged abuse of company funds.
-- Sales of office space rose 18 percent in 1996 in the Paris area.
-- Regional newspaper L'Est Republicain to buy Les Dernieres Nouvelles d'Alsace.
L'AGEFI
-- Paribas posts record profit partly due to capital gains.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Study shows state-owned companies suffer from their special retirement schemes which prove much costlier than the private sector's.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis says earnings from privatisations implemented in 1996 and 1997 would cover recapitalisations planned for 1997, notably that of GAN.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Renault closes plant in Belgium, plans to concentrate production in France.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Small expansion for Q4 French GDP, up 0.2 percent, spurs hope for 1997.
